title: Congress Builds Big Lead Over BJP in Rajasthan Panchayat Polls as Counting Continues
excerpt: With counting still under way across 37 districts, Congress had won 2,990 Panchayat Samiti and 143 Zila Parishad seats in declared results, against 1,795 and 83 for the ruling BJP.
body:
• Congress is well ahead of the ruling BJP in Rajasthan's panchayat elections, with 2,990 Panchayat Samiti seats and 143 Zila Parishad seats in results declared so far, against the BJP's 1,795 and 83.
  • Counting on Friday covered 7,543 Panchayat Samiti and 1,275 Zila Parishad seats across 37 of the state's 41 districts; results in four districts are deferred to December 17.
  • Congress took Jaipur's Zila Parishad count with 34 of the 46 wards declared, and won Bharatpur and Churu, while the RLP finished first in Nagaur and the BJP held Ajmer.
  • The elections were held in four phases on October 22, October 28, November 3 and November 14, with more than 2.48 crore votes polled in the 37 districts counted on Friday.

The Congress built a substantial lead over the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party as counting continued on Friday in Rajasthan's Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti elections, outperforming the BJP in both tiers of the state's rural local bodies.

In results declared so far, according to State Election Commission figures reported in the Daily Jagran's live coverage, the Congress had won 2,990 Panchayat Samiti seats and 143 Zila Parishad seats. The BJP had secured 1,795 Panchayat Samiti seats and 83 Zila Parishad seats. Independents had won 516 Panchayat Samiti seats and five Zila Parishad seats, the Rashtriya Loktantrik Party (RLP) 438 and four, the Bharat Adivasi Party 215 Panchayat Samiti seats, the CPI(M) 50 and three, the BSP 44 and one, and the AAP two Panchayat Samiti seats. Counting was still under way when those figures were reported, and they are declared results, not final totals.

The scale of the count

Counting covered 7,543 Panchayat Samiti seats and 1,275 Zila Parishad seats across 37 of Rajasthan's 41 districts, with 25,108 candidates in the Panchayat Samiti contests and 4,069 in the Zila Parishad wards, spread across 419 Panchayat Samitis. Results in Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sri Ganganagar have been deferred to December 17, because the five-year terms of the existing local bodies there expire in December. The four-phase elections were held on October 22, October 28, November 3 and November 14, and more than 2.48 crore votes were polled at 41,480 polling stations in the 37 districts counted on Friday.

How the big districts went

In Jaipur, the Congress won 34 of the 46 Zila Parishad wards declared, against 10 for the BJP and two for the RLP, with 11 of the council's 57 wards still to be declared, according to Jagran Josh's results coverage. Congress secured 21 of 31 seats in Bharatpur, where the BJP won nine, and 21 of 39 in Churu, where the BJP won 17. In Nagaur, the RLP emerged as the largest party with 19 of 37 seats, ahead of the Congress on 11 and the BJP on seven. The BJP's clearest district win came in Ajmer, where it took 19 of 33 seats against 12 for the Congress and two for the RLP.

At the samiti level, the Daily Jagran reported that the Congress had won 213 of the 419 Panchayat Samitis, compared with 85 for the BJP and 56 for Independents, and that the BJP suffered setbacks in several of its strongholds, including Chittorgarh, Sirohi, Rajsamand and Jalore, while the Congress made gains in Jaipur, Jodhpur, Bikaner and Bhilwara.

What it means

The results are a setback for the BJP government of Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma in the first statewide rural test covered in this count, and a strong showing for the opposition Congress in the bodies that run village-level administration across most of the state. Panchayat Samitis and Zila Parishads control local development work and welfare delivery, so control of them shapes both parties' ground organisation well beyond the count itself.

What happens next

Counting for the remaining seats continues, and the four deferred districts vote-count on December 17. The newly elected Zila Parishad members will then elect their Zila Pramukhs; in Jaipur, that vote is scheduled for November 25, according to Jagran Josh. Final statewide totals will only be settled once the deferred districts are counted.
